scope.basis: User corrected scope to four current repositories; audit and bounded fixes were requested in the attached autonomous engineering instructions.
scope.preservedConcurrentWork: Core advanced from 7050cdb to 684b459 through another documentation-only commit during the audit. Its two files were preserved. Final core verification ran after that commit.

method.execution: Inline investigation, implementation and separate adversarial review; workspace instructions prohibit subagents. No independent-agent review is claimed.
method.coverage: Risk-focused source review and whole default repository suites, followed by targeted database/browser integration. This is not a line-by-line proof of all code or exhaustive live-service qualification.

outcome.sourceFixesPushed: Core and frontend dev; remote heads read back after push. Modules and landing have no audit source changes.

findings.title: A delayed Anchor connection could undo disconnect or replace a newer payer
findings.trigger: Start a native connection, then disconnect, change account/network/RPC/API scope, or finish a newer connection before the older approval returns.
findings.rootCause: connectNative assigned nativeWallet after asynchronous work without invalidating a superseded connection intent.
findings.impact: Stale wallet state and wrong displayed payer identity. No unauthorized transaction was established; existing wallet approval and spending checks remain.
findings.change: Capture a monotonic connection revision and current workspace/API scope; check after network lookup and wallet approval. Disconnect increments the revision.

evidence.counterfactual: The final eight-case regression fixture against baseline source produced seven failures and one normal-success pass. Restoring the fix produced eight passes.

findings.limits: SessionKit/Session objects are real; external approval and the renderer are controlled. Real Anchor transport, prompt cancellation and SDK persisted metadata are not qualified.

findings.title: Failed rollback hid the original shared transaction failure
findings.trigger: An operation or COMMIT fails and ROLLBACK also fails.
findings.rootCause: The cleanup await threw before the original error or LAST_CONTROL_CREDENTIAL mapping could propagate.
findings.impact: Incorrect error reporting and loss of the original diagnostic/business error. Data corruption and unsafe pool reuse were not established; pg-pool already removes known non-queryable clients.
findings.change: Preserve the original failure, retain the constraint mapping, and release once with explicit client destruction after failed rollback.

evidence.redResult: Three failures and two passes before the repair.
evidence.greenResult: All five cases passed: failed cleanup, success, ordinary rollback, failed commit and credential mapping.

findings.limits: Cleanup faults are transport injections; PostgreSQL integration exercises real account/recovery constraints without deliberately killing a production database connection.

findings.title: Email pairing browser test expected a collapsed row to remain visible
findings.trigger: The real API accepts an email pairing; awaitingCode becomes false and the Email details closes.
findings.rootCause: The test did not reopen the existing panel before asserting the paired row is visible. Baseline product code contains the same closing behavior.
findings.change: Click the Email summary after the pairing success notice; retain the visible paired-address assertion and same-account passkey login checks.

evidence.result: Both desktop/mobile Chromium journeys passed against the real API and fresh PostgreSQL after the one-line test interaction fix.

decisions.alternatives: Patching every caller would duplicate cancellation behavior. SDK-wide cancellation/persistence changes require actual wallet lifecycle qualification and are outside the proven app-state defect.

decisions.chosen: Repair the existing shared withTransaction helper
decisions.alternatives: Changing only individual auth callers leaves the shared cause. Rewriting every content/payment/migration transaction requires separate tracing and fault tests; it is not needed to repair this helper.

decisions.chosen: Preserve current producer/consumer boundaries and frozen historical fixtures
decisions.alternatives: File size alone does not prove a design defect. No speculative splitting, dependency replacement or history regeneration was justified.

verification.qualification: The release manifest still reports publication refused and qualified false; this expected gate remains. Passing verify does not establish a publishable release.

verification.warning: Existing chunks exceed the 500 kB warning. Runtime load/bundle profiling was not performed; no limit was weakened.

verification.limits: Registry advisory check, not a proof that dependencies are secure.

remaining.topic: Explicit transaction cleanup outside the shared helper
remaining.evidence: services/api/src/auth.ts:156 and services/api/src/creation.ts:278 still await ROLLBACK before rethrowing the original error. Additional raw rollback calls exist in storage/content/payment/migration paths; not every call is an error cleanup.
remaining.risk: The same simultaneous-failure error masking can remain in these paths. No data-loss or pool-contamination claim is made.
remaining.next: Trace each transaction and add path-specific failure injections before consolidating or repairing its cleanup; preserve accounting and migration behavior.

remaining.evidence: The build emits a chunk-size warning. Large source files alone were not classified as bugs.
remaining.unrun: Production traffic, database query plans under realistic load, long-running worker behavior, full bundle/runtime performance and new RAM/CPU profiling.

setupCorrections: An initial frontend API-change fixture changed an unloaded environment value; it was corrected to use actual configured API endpoints. The final counterfactual validates the corrected fixture.
Test-only Promise.withResolvers conflicted with the frontend ES2022 TypeScript library and was replaced with an ordinary deferred promise.
The pg overloaded connect mock needed mockImplementation instead of a void-inferred mockResolvedValue.
The local PostgreSQL CLI required its existing shared-library path; all actual test databases were owned and dropped.
Git lacked author configuration; commit-local Codex identity matching prior commits was used. No global Git configuration was changed.

compatibilityAndRollback.interfaces: Existing connectNative/disconnectNative and withTransaction signatures, protocol/ABI/public pins, authorization constraints, account IDs and persisted schemas are unchanged.
compatibilityAndRollback.operationalEffect: Stale native connections reject instead of assigning wallet state; consumers already handle rejected connections. Shared transactions keep their original error and discard after failed cleanup.
compatibilityAndRollback.rollback: Review and revert source fix commits on dev if needed. No data migration, native action or deployed-service rollback is required by these changes.

recommendedNextWork: Qualify real wallet cancellation/connection lifecycle and source-bound release suites; then fault-test the remaining explicit transaction cleanup. Profile actual bundle/database/worker load before structural optimization.
decisionsRequired: No additional policy decision is required for the completed bounded repairs. A new deployment or production asset/authority operation remains subject to explicit user authorization.
